_schema: Session 44 verb seeds. pres = [ich,du,er,wir,ihr,sie] of the BASE verb (without separable prefix). praet = 6 forms (strong) or the ich-form string (weak). sent: p = person key or 'inf'; 'X ... Y' marks a separable split across two blanks. tdist = 3 English meanings that are NOT synonyms. refl = reflexive pronouns used in conjugation tables (only for verbs that are always reflexive). standalone = prefix verb whose base verb the app does not teach (served in Variationen).

sent.en: The film lasts two hours.

sent.de: Wie lange _____ die Fahrt nach Hamburg?
sent.en: How long does the drive to Hamburg take?
The construction work will take another three weeks.

roots.trans_note: Impersonal with time: Es dauert lange. B1/B2 synonym: anhalten.

gram.notes_en: dauern has no object; the duration is an accusative of time: Das dauert eine Stunde.

sent.en: We often talk about politics.
You talk too fast!
My grandpa likes talking about the old days.

roots.trans_note: More colloquial than sprechen. reden über + Akk, reden mit + Dat.

gram.notes_en: reden über + Akkusativ (about), reden mit + Dativ (with).

roots.english: to report / (sich) to get in touch

sent.en: I'll get in touch with you tomorrow.

sent.de: Der Nachbar _____ den Unfall der Polizei.
sent.en: The neighbour reports the accident to the police.
Why do you never get in touch?

roots.trans_note: sich melden (bei + Dat) = to get in touch.

gram.notes_en: etwas (Akk) jemandem (Dat) melden = to report something to someone. sich bei jemandem melden = to get in touch with someone.

sent.en: I keep having to sneeze.
My brother always sneezes three times in a row.
With hay fever we sneeze a lot.

roots.trans_note: When someone sneezes, Germans say: Gesundheit!

gram.notes_en: No object. Partizip II: geniest.

sent.en: We laugh at the joke.
Why are you laughing?
The baby laughs all day.

roots.trans_note: lachen über + Akk = to laugh at/about. Not lächeln (to smile).

gram.notes_en: lachen über + Akkusativ = to laugh at something.

sent.de: Der Kellner kommt, wenn du mit den Fingern _____.
sent.en: The waiter comes when you snap your fingers.
I snap my fingers to the beat of the music.

sent.de: Die Zuschauer _____ mit den Fingern, statt zu klatschen.
sent.en: The audience snap their fingers instead of clapping.

roots.trans_note: mit den Fingern schnipsen. (The source image wrote 'schipsen' — that is not a German word.)

gram.notes_en: Usually: mit den Fingern schnipsen. Transitive = to flick: Er schnipst die Krümel vom Tisch.

sent.en: In the cinema we only whisper.

sent.de: Ich _____ dir ein Geheimnis ins Ohr.
sent.en: I whisper a secret in your ear.
Why are you all whispering?

roots.trans_note: Opposite: schreien (to shout).

gram.notes_en: Can take what is whispered (Akk) and a listener (Dat): Ich flüstere dir etwas ins Ohr.

sent.en: My father snores every night.

sent.de: Du _____ so laut, ich kann nicht schlafen!
sent.en: You snore so loudly, I can't sleep!

sent.de: Ich _____ nur, wenn ich erkältet bin.
sent.en: I only snore when I have a cold.

gram.notes_en: No object.

sent.en: The child has been coughing for three days.
I cough all night.
Why are you coughing so much?

roots.trans_note: der Husten = the cough.

gram.notes_en: No object.

sent.de: Am Ende des Konzerts _____ alle Zuschauer.
sent.en: At the end of the concert all the spectators clap.
I clap my hands.
Why aren't you all clapping?

roots.trans_note: Colloquially also: to gossip (über jemanden klatschen).

gram.notes_en: in die Hände klatschen = to clap one's hands.

sent.en: The dog farts in its sleep.
I never fart in public.
We all fart sometimes.

roots.trans_note: Vulgar — with friends only.

gram.notes_en: Vulgar register. der Furz = the fart.

roots.english: to search for (police) / to hunt for

sent.en: The police are searching for the perpetrator.

sent.de: Wir _____ seit Wochen nach dem Fehler.
sent.en: We have been hunting for the bug for weeks.

sent.de: Die Ermittler _____ europaweit nach dem Mann.
sent.en: The investigators are searching for the man all over Europe.

roots.trans_note: fahnden nach + Dativ — mostly police/official language.

gram.notes_en: fahnden nach + Dativ. die Fahndung = the manhunt.

sent.en: I'm afraid of big dogs.
Many people dread winter.
My brother is afraid of spiders.

roots.trans_note: sich fürchten vor + Dativ = to be afraid of. Everyday: Angst haben vor.

gram.notes_en: etwas (Akk) fürchten = to fear something; sich vor + Dativ fürchten = to be afraid of.

sent.de: Ich _____ dich: Das Eis ist dünn!
sent.en: I'm warning you: the ice is thin!
The weather service warns of a storm.

sent.de: Die Ärzte _____ vor zu viel Zucker.
sent.en: Doctors warn against too much sugar.

roots.trans_note: jemanden vor + Dativ warnen.

gram.notes_en: jemanden (Akk) vor etwas (Dat) warnen.

sent.en: The family is fleeing from the war.

sent.de: Der Gefangene konnte aus dem Gefängnis _____.
sent.en: The prisoner was able to escape from prison.

sent.de: Wir _____ vor dem Regen ins Café.
sent.en: We flee from the rain into the café.

roots.trans_note: Not fliegen (to fly)! fliehen – floh – ist geflohen.

gram.notes_en: fliehen vor + Dativ (from a danger), fliehen aus + Dativ (out of a place).

sent.en: Sunscreen protects the skin.
I protect myself with a mask.

sent.de: Wir _____ die Pflanzen vor dem Frost.
sent.en: We protect the plants from the frost.

roots.trans_note: jemanden/etwas vor + Dativ schützen. der Schutz = protection.

gram.notes_en: etwas (Akk) vor etwas (Dat) schützen.

sent.en: I'm surprised by his behaviour.
That doesn't surprise me.
We're surprised that nobody is coming.

roots.trans_note: sich wundern über + Akk. Don't confuse with bewundern (to admire).

gram.notes_en: Etwas wundert mich (Akk) = something surprises me; sich über + Akk wundern = to be surprised at.

roots.english: (sich) to be patient / to wait patiently

sent.en: Please be patient for a moment.

sent.de: Ich _____ mich, bis du fertig bist.
sent.en: I'll be patient until you're done.
You have to be patient a little longer.

roots.trans_note: Always reflexive: sich gedulden. From die Geduld (patience). B1/B2 alternative to warten.

gram.notes_en: Always reflexive with an accusative pronoun: Ich gedulde mich. Formal request: Bitte gedulden Sie sich.

roots.english: to cope with / to manage / to overcome

sent.en: We'll overcome this crisis together.
How do you manage so much work?
I can't manage that alone.

roots.trans_note: Inseparable (be-): Partizip II without ge- — bewältigt.

gram.notes_en: Takes an accusative object: eine Aufgabe bewältigen.

sent.en: The contract guarantees our security.
We have to ensure quality.
The companies ensure secure data protection.

roots.trans_note: Formal. Compound of die Gewähr + leisten, never splits: gewährleistet.

gram.notes_en: Takes an accusative object. Never separates.

sent.en: The noise impairs my concentration.

sent.de: Zu wenig Schlaf kann die Gesundheit _____.
sent.en: Too little sleep can impair your health.
The construction work affects the traffic.

roots.trans_note: Formal. Inseparable: beeinträchtigt.

gram.notes_en: Takes an accusative object.

sent.en: The chart illustrates the results.
I'll illustrate that with an example.
Can you illustrate that, please?

roots.trans_note: From the adjective anschaulich (vivid, clear).

gram.notes_en: Takes an accusative object.

sent.en: We analyse the data.
The doctor analyses the blood.
You always analyse everything too closely.

roots.trans_note: -ieren verbs take no ge- in the Partizip II: analysiert.

gram.notes_en: Takes an accusative object.

sent.en: I intend to move next year.
What do you intend by that?

sent.de: Die Regierung _____, die Steuern zu senken.
sent.en: The government intends to lower taxes.

roots.trans_note: Formal. Everyday: vorhaben. From die Absicht (intention).

gram.notes_en: Takes an accusative object or a zu-infinitive.

sent.de: Ich _____ mich gern an meine Kindheit.
sent.en: I like remembering my childhood.

sent.de: Das Lied _____ mich an den Sommer.
sent.en: The song reminds me of summer.

sent.de: Wir _____ uns kaum an den Unfall.
sent.en: We barely remember the accident.

roots.trans_note: sich erinnern an + Akk = to remember; jemanden an etwas erinnern = to remind someone of something.

gram.notes_en: jemanden (Akk) an etwas (Akk) erinnern. Reflexive: sich an + Akkusativ erinnern.

sent.en: I just don't get it.
Finally he grasps the rule.
Children catch on quickly.

roots.trans_note: Inseparable (be- + greifen). B1/B2 alternative to verstehen.

gram.notes_en: Takes an accusative object. Strong: begriff – begriffen.

sent.en: I need your help.

sent.de: Für den Antrag _____ man einen Pass.
sent.en: For the application you need a passport.
We still need two chairs.

roots.trans_note: More formal than brauchen.

gram.notes_en: Takes an accusative object, like brauchen.

roots.english: to prompt / to arrange for / to cause

sent.en: What prompts you to make this decision?
I'll arrange for an inspection immediately.

sent.de: Die Ergebnisse _____ uns, den Plan zu ändern.
sent.en: The results prompt us to change the plan.

roots.trans_note: Formal. Inseparable: veranlasst. der Anlass = the occasion/reason.

gram.notes_en: jemanden (Akk) zu etwas (Dat) veranlassen = to prompt someone to do something.

roots.english: to understand / to follow (a line of reasoning)

sent.en: I can understand your decision well.
Nobody follows his logic.
I don't follow the thought.

roots.trans_note: Separable: Ich vollziehe das nach. Most common with können: Das kann ich nachvollziehen.

gram.notes_en: Takes an accusative object. Separable, strong: nachvollzogen.

sent.en: How do you assess the situation?
Experts have to assess the risk precisely.
I judge him to be very honest.

roots.trans_note: Separable: Ich schätze das anders ein.

gram.notes_en: Takes an accusative object; als + adjective for the judgement.

roots.english: to admit (formal) / to grant / to put away (into)

sent.en: The minister admits his mistake.
I load the dishwasher.
We grant you more time.

roots.trans_note: Separable. Formal 'admit'; everyday: zugeben.

gram.notes_en: jemandem (Dat) etwas (Akk) einräumen = to grant someone something.

sent.en: We always go away in summer.
I'd like to go away again soon.
You're going away over Easter, right?

attach.notes: Inseparable (ver- never detaches). Perfekt with sein: Ich bin verreist = I'm away.

attach.english: to drop by / to pass by

sent.en: I'll drop by briefly tomorrow.
The bus passes by here every hour.
When are you dropping by?

attach.notes: Separable: Ich komme vorbei. Perfekt with sein. B1/B2 alternative to besuchen.

sent.en: I'll look it up in the dictionary.

sent.de: Kannst du bitte _____, ob die Tür zu ist?
sent.en: Can you please check whether the door is closed?
The mechanic checks the oil.

attach.notes: Separable. Also: jemandem nachsehen = to watch someone leave.

sent.en: I find out the truth.
We have to find out who that was.
The police find out the reason.

attach.notes: Separable. Colloquial short form: rausfinden (Ich finde das raus).

sent.en: This job requires good German skills.
I take that as known.
Many courses presuppose prior knowledge.

attach.notes: Separable. Common: vorausgesetzt, dass … = provided that …

sent.en: I'll go on ahead.
The argument is preceded by a misunderstanding.
We're going ahead today; you'll come later.

attach.notes: Separable. Perfekt with sein. etwas (Dat) vorausgehen = to precede something.

sent.en: Sport compensates for the stress.
We have to make up for the losses.
I balance out the deficit.

attach.english: to strive for / to aim for

sent.de: Ich _____ eine Karriere in der Forschung _____.
sent.en: I'm aiming for a career in research.
The company is aiming for more revenue.
We strive for a peaceful solution.

attach.notes: Separable and transitive (+ Akk) — same meaning as streben nach + Dativ.
